question.text: Let $S, T, U$ be three non-void sets and $f: S \rightarrow T, g: T \rightarrow U$ be so that $g o f: s \rightarrow U$ is surjective. Then,

options.text: $g$ is surjective, $f$ may not be so
$f$ is surjective, $g$ may not be so
$f$ and $g$ both may not be surjective

solution.text:

$\Rightarrow g(y)=Z,$ where $y=f(x) \in T$ for all $Z \in U$
